document.title: Colonel Tsagolov's Letter to USSR Minister of Defense Dmitry Yazov on the Situation in Afghanistan, August 13, 1987
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan: Lessons from the Last War
document.note: Criticism of the policy of national reconciliation and analysis of the failures of the Soviet military mission. It was the first open criticism of the war from within the military; Tsagolov was expelled from the Army in 1988 after an Ogonek interview.

events.description: Colonel Tsagolov writes to Defense Minister Yazov criticizing Soviet strategy and national reconciliation in Afghanistan and proposing new steps before withdrawal.
Founding of the PDPA as combination of Khalq and Parcham.

National reconciliation policy announced by the Afghan leadership, with a coalition government proposal.
Soviet leadership announces strategic decision to withdraw the limited contingent from the DRA.

key_claims: Soviet efforts over eight years failed to stabilize Afghanistan and the problem cannot be solved by military means alone.
National reconciliation failed to win mass, party, or counter-revolutionary support and the opposition intends to take power by force.
The regime has no serious positions in the kishlak (rural) zone, which is controlled by counter-revolutionary forces.
The PDPA is an artificial Khalq-Parcham combination moving toward political death and Najib cannot save it.
A coalition government with Zahir Shah or any combination of the Peshawar 'seven' would not solve the situation.
The mujahideen are aware of the Soviet decision to withdraw and will not accept partial power.
Desertions in the Afghan army are growing and could become massive after the reconciliation period.
